title.narrative: PIMS- 9706-Support and build a more Sustainable Blue Economy in Aqaba through Marine Spatial Planning (MSP) and effective management of the first marine reserve in the country

description.narrative: Aqaba Special Economic Zone Authority lacks a sustainable blue economy (SBE) framework resulting in competing activities adding pressures on vulnerable marine resources. The project shall develop a Marine Spatial Plan within the Aqaba Special Economic Zone for official adoption. It shall act as a tool for conservation, restoration and sustainable management, to build resilience of Jordan’s marine ecosystem. This shift from the business as usual approach will support more sustainable investments, benefitting peoples well-being, and contributing to the GEF8 Focal Area Biodiversity strategy and GEF CI 5, 6 and 11. It shall enhance coral and seagrass management for carbon sequestration, generating ecosystem services, protecting wildlife, and securing local economies. The project will benefit 188,160 people living in Aqaba, 50% being women. It will contribute to the CBD goals and the KM GBF targets 1, 2, 3, 7, 11, 19 and 20 whilst supporting SDG 14 and delivery of GEB for biodiversity and climate change. Expected results include: i) a formally mandated SBE institutional, policy and legislative framework strengthening capacities and private sector engagement ii) improved business partnerships supported by financially innovative incentive mechanisms iii) improved marine ecosystem resilience to climate change/disasters and iv) a new research agenda created with M&E processes to assess project related performance.

condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

The Implementing Partner shall ensure that all of its obligations set forth under the section entitled “Legal Context and/or Risk Management Standard Clauses” are passed on to each responsible party, subcontractor and sub-recipient and that all the clauses under this section entitled “Risk Management” are included, mutatis mutandis, in all sub-contracts or sub-agreements entered into further to the Project Document
